Yea I use kodi as the main media viewing application but on top of ubuntu.

By 10 foot interface really what I mean is an operating system that can easily be used from the sofa, windows (or 9x GUI design philosophy in general) doesn't tend to lend itself to this. It's mainly tweaks to button sizes but it boils down to a lot of UI decisions e.g. it is easier to have analogue 'left' or 'right' options rather than things requiring mouse precision.

I've started with ubuntu as it runs most things and following various tweaks (e.g. here: http://www.libregeek.org/2013/12/23/how-to-making-a-media-center-using-ubuntu-12-04-lts/) I've got it to an okay state, but what would be really cool is a custom distro specifically designed and pre-tweaked for use from the couch. Yeah, I hear ya on kodi's limitations. Its got grand ambitions that it hits about 80%.

Anyway, I did a similar project before switching to kodi (then xbmc) based on Fedora, but was using a full desktop machine that's since been repurposed. When I was using it, I had a custom KDE environment w/ a bunch of media-centric widgets that I would control from a wireless USB mouse.

At one point I had a "launcher" widget on the desktop that was actually just a bunch of shortcuts to web video like YT, JTV (when that existed), Daily Show, MLB.tv (with proxy route-around for geoblocking), ESPN3 and others. Was very cool to use from the couch, but also unreliable due to the nature of the web.

Unfortunately, KDE is going through an upgrade cycle this year, so the old multimedia and launcher widgets are no longer supported, and new widgets aren't quite there. And kodi is completing its transition from xbmc (they'll claim they're done, but the plugin selection says otherwise). There are companies producing "media centers" based on "linux", but those are actually kodi machines.

I say hold tight and check back on linux multimedia in six months. I see two things happening: 1) kodi gets its shit together, and B) someone else recognizes this gap and launches a new 'couch linux' distro.
